campaign: Integrate native MOSS-Image-SFT generation and deterministic model import

paragraphs.text: overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is each scorecard cell against its previous measurement, not a count of landings: there is no passed state and no promotion. Rows that let a full measurement run finish rank above rows that only harden or slim it, and a run that cannot finish (killed, or with cells that did not pass) outranks every other row.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and the cycle runs them on the commit it measures; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

User-journey performance (owner, 2026-10-05). Optimize complete journeys, measured as action to usable result: submit to first visible answer, cold model selection to usable response, cancel to actual resource release, interrupted cycle to useful progress, with loading, admission wait, execution, publication and rendering kept apart. Start from the existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles of repeated reads, model loads, allocations and evidence reconstruction, and keep added instrumentation only when it explains a real elapsed-time gain. In the development loop one valid gate execution is shared by every compatible plan step and obligation, and validation and reuse are scoped by the actual dependencies (kernels, generated and embedded data, models, recipes, environment, subprocess effects); an unknown dependency keeps the broader coverage. A gain is judged against total maintenance cost (production code, tests, fixtures, instrumentation, gate work and upkeep): remove repeated processing through existing owners, and decline small gains that need disproportionate machinery. Prove with behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, never a new performance ratchet, selector or framework.

Pace (owner, 2026-10-09). Steps that change one mechanism land together. A measurement already taken retires the step that would take it. Work that only waits is filed early, so its wait runs while the rows between are built. A full measurement run (go run ./cmd/loop -improve) continues only at the commit it began at and is started outside a session, so no time limit ends it. Rows that move no measured result land while it runs; rows that change a served result or a timing follow it, stand side by side, and land before the next run, never between its runs.

The repository keeps Go, CUDA and HTML/JS, and extends an existing owner before it adds one. Each row begins with a measurement and fixes its acceptance before its code is written; a measurement already taken is reused when it is enough. A row deletes the implementation it replaces in the same landing; a reader that records already in the store need stays until those records are migrated. A pilot that is not accepted is taken out of the served path, and its measurements and the reason it was refused are kept.

The production growth refusal stays. A row with no count adds no net production code, which is the default: a migration deletes at least what it adds. A row that adds a mechanism before it deletes one carries a count, set in a change to the plan alone before its code, from the figure the gate's preflight gives its built change, and read from the commit the change builds on; a count set before the row is built is an estimate and says so. An item's count is for all its landings together: each landing's growth is charged to it and what is left is what the next may add. Test code, fixtures, record schemas and CUDA source are reported with each landing and not refused; a test is retired only when its replacement catches the same seeded failure.

The gate judges the candidate tree by hermetic and small-device checks; real-model quality and speed are measured by the cycle. A stored result is reused only under an unchanged identity of the code, model, recipe, data, settings and request it depends on. A request for a fresh measurement always runs, and a dependency that cannot be named keeps the wider scope. Resident resources, compiled execution and a request have separate identities, built by one mechanism into separate keys for sessions, outputs and scores. Eligibility is kept apart from selection, observations from scores, and the records that choose a candidate from the records that confirm it.

An experiment is frozen before it trains: a protocol missing a numerical gain or resource criterion is not dispatched, and a pilot does not change the acceptance of the objective it is compared with. Completing an experiment and adopting its model are separate: a complete negative or inconclusive record closes the experiment and activates nothing.

Each iteration integrates current master, updates the plan from evidence, implements the next coherent steps and commits through the landing gate.
This worktree retains its MOSS plan when integrating master code.
Other components enter this plan only when required by a MOSS acceptance obligation.
Training, LoRA, image-to-image, video and automatic prompt enhancement are outside this campaign.
Base acquisition and serving are outside this campaign.

Pinned model_index.json declares MOSSImagePipeline, MOSSImageTransformer, MOSSImageScheduler, Qwen3_5Model, Qwen2Tokenizer and AutoencoderKLFlux2.
The transformer config declares 42 layers, hidden width 3072, FFN width 8192, 24 heads, text width 4096, timestep frequency width 256 and 128 packed latent channels.
The text encoder config declares 32 hybrid linear/full-attention layers with hidden width 4096; reuse Overgo's Qwen3.5 execution where its hidden-state contract matches.
The bundled VAE has 32 latent channels, a 2-by-2 latent patch, batch-normalization statistics and the small decoder widths [96,192,384,384]; the current latentimage QwenImage VAE and selected-layer Qwen3-VL conditioner are not drop-in implementations.
Pinned SFT safetensors sizes are 16785478992 bytes for the text encoder, 10164664216 bytes for the transformer and 249521372 bytes for the VAE: 27199664580 bytes before tokenizer, metadata, runtime buffers or caches.
Only the SFT checkpoint is an acquisition, serving and evaluation target; previously collected Base metadata remains historical reference material.
Resident inference memory is unmeasured and must include activations, attention workspace, decoder buffers, graph allocations and host staging; the 5B marketing size describes the transformer rather than the complete pipeline.

Parity targets the pinned released pipeline, not an unavailable training-time fp32-master implementation.
Default workload uses a CPU generator seeded with 42, 1024-by-1024 output, 50 requested steps, guidance 3, shift 5, empty negative prompt and negative-branch skip index 22.
MOSSImageScheduler snaps shifted sigmas to the nearest training grid and removes consecutive duplicates, so actual step count must come from the resulting schedule.
The pipeline wraps prompts with apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=true, enable_thinking=true), runs individual unpadded encoder forwards with use_cache=false, and consumes last_hidden_state with a true-length mask.
DiT and conditioner use bf16; initial noise, prediction combination, Euler updates and VAE decoding use fp32; timestep sinusoids use fp64 before conversion and RoPE frequencies and phases use fp32.
Dimensions are positive multiples of 16 and prompt maximum length is 4096; preserve or explicitly expose upstream truncation rather than silently rewriting prompts.
Default CFG performs two transformer forwards per step; guidance 1 removes the negative branch.
Optional positive-branch SLG adds another forward and is deferred; unsupported controls must be rejected rather than silently ignored.
Deterministic import means the same pinned bytes and policy produce the same content identities, tensor mappings and recipe; it does not promise GPU bit identity across hardware or library versions.
Freeze numerical tolerance from independently measured oracle repeatability and datatype effects before comparing native outputs; do not widen it to accept a failed port.

Reuse artifact, hfhub, hfrepo, safetensors, tensorcatalog, modelartifact, modelintake, libraryintake and modelrecipe for acquisition, inventory, lifecycle and capability publication.
Extend the existing intake operation and CLI surfaces instead of adding a MOSS-only downloader, registry or serving process.
Keep architecture facts and defaults in versioned artifacts and recipes; implement missing numerical operations in the existing tensor, graph and media owners.
Generalize only where MOSS and a second real supported model demonstrate the same contract; preserve distinct conditioner, transformer, scheduler and decoder semantics.
Apply the broader Strata direction through exact dependency identities, stage-local execution, bounded residency and reuse of valid intermediate results, without inventing a parallel graph or cache framework.
Training-time gains are not an acceptance claim for this inference campaign.
Verification selectors below name acceptance work to be added by their rows; they are not claims that tests already exist or passed.
Use cmd/plan or the landing gate to execute row verifiers so missing tests and skips are rejected as vacuous evidence.
Hermetic and small-device parity belongs to the landing gate; full weight loads, quality sets and performance runs belong to the model-tagged improvement cycle.
Production syntax-node counts below are planning estimates for new behavior, not measured performance targets; narrow them when the first implementation diff establishes the required scope.

The overgo_moss plan owns MOSS image generation and deterministic import.
Integrating master code never replaces this plan with master campaign rows or removes MOSS validation evidence.
Shared-component work names the MOSS obligation it serves and extends the existing owner.
Completed acquisition and oracle work stays retired under its landed evidence.
Structural import inspection does not establish numerical parity or serving activation.

items.title: Mechanize inspection and materialization through existing intake

budget.reason: The 6000-node importer allowance retains 569 nodes after 4523 inspection nodes, 118 streaming nodes, 346 source-verification nodes and 444 replay nodes measured by preflight. Remaining work reuses existing publication and lifecycle owners.

steps.title: Execute an import description idempotently and retain rollback
steps.rationale:
Execute the frozen description using bounded streaming reads, existing artifact publication and exact tensor transforms; preserve native safetensors when conversion has no demonstrated consumer.
Keep acquire, verify, prepare, validate and activate as durable lifecycle states under existing owners.
Deduplicate verified SFT components across retries and existing cached artifacts by content and atomically publish a candidate only when all references resolve.
Cancellation, restart and repeated import must reuse verified chunks and produce the same logical artifact identity; a failed write must never become verified state.
An import can be complete while serving remains unverified; activation requires the later numerical and capability evidence, with rollback to the previous activation.
Test corruption, interrupted conversion, duplicate retries, stale verification, disk failure and missing component without touching a live store.
Serves: reliable operator and unattended model intake.
Disappears: bespoke installer state and duplicate component copies through artifact/modelintake lifecycle reuse.
Evidence: import receipt and candidate lineage read by library, recipe and final validation.
Batch: intake, lifecycle and API lanes; activation changes may expire execution guards and require media reconciliation.
Compose the import description from existing manifests, TensorInventoryDocument, architecture profiles, resolved model definitions and recipe graphs.
Do not create a second registry or parallel import state machine.
Existing stage receipts retain progress and failures, artifact.Publish commits atomic batches, and recipe activation retains rollback.
Reuse requires identical source, mapping, transformation, policy and validation identities.
Locations and transient transfer state do not enter logical content identities.
Acquired, structurally valid, numerically verified and activated states remain distinct.
A new document contract is justified only by a fact the existing records cannot represent.

Only declared and shape-verified language weights enter resident execution while inventory accounts for unused visual components.

Disappears: a separate MOSS text decoder and production diagnostic executor; existing tokenizer, HF mapping, compiled model programs, tensor operations and media bindings own execution.

items.title: Implement the MOSS transformer in the native graph

budget.reason: Missing text refinement, shared modulation and bounded SITU arithmetic are expected; reuse existing attention, normalization, linear and graph kernels.

steps.title: Compile rotary text refinement through the existing image graph owner
steps.rationale:
Serves: the MOSS transformer text-refinement stage independently of unresolved conditioner arithmetic.
Disappears: a separate text-refinement executor through existing FusionProgram, tensor operators, resident graph binding and CUDA execution.
Evidence: frozen native small-model fixtures for both refinement blocks and complete text projection, plus source-bound real-model CUDA stage comparisons.
Batch: graph and image lanes with inference surface guard expiry.
The two biased refinement blocks use ordinary learned RMSNorm, per-head query/key normalization, supplied half-split rotary coefficients, bidirectional attention and bounded SITU.
BF16 storage rounds follow native operator boundaries rather than changing every activation type.
The new compiler uses existing weight bindings and resident execution.
A model-lane consumer exercises real-checkpoint execution before the complete generator is available.
Require exact source and input identities and keep CPU and CUDA comparison contracts distinct.
Complete denoiser integration, all-block execution, branch skipping and full-image parity remain in forward.
The existing 1800-node transformer allowance remains an estimate until preflight measures the implementation.
The acquired native small-device fixture reveals BF16 unnormalized softmax probabilities with F32 normalization.
All 96 isolated attention outputs match that arithmetic exactly while normalized BF16 probabilities and F32-only probabilities fail bitwise comparison.
Extend the existing 128-channel BF16 attention tile to zero-fill narrower heads in its shared-memory stage rather than introduce another kernel or pad complete activations.
The 16-byte asynchronous transfer requires head widths divisible by eight.
Preserve the 128-channel dispatch and allocation contract and validate narrow-head bounds, repeatability, existing device attention, and native refinement goldens.
Kernel source and binary identities must be regenerated together.

steps.title: Match transformer arithmetic and branch skipping
steps.rationale:
Represent the two text-refinement blocks, image-then-text joint attention, four-coordinate RoPE, fp64-to-fp32 timestep embedding, shared six-way modulation, RMSNorm and bounded SITU FFN using typed recipe-selected operators.
Derive geometry and parameter bindings from the import description, including bias distinctions and full tensor coverage.
Preserve fp32 RoPE construction before bf16 activation casts; do not reuse a superficially similar SwiGLU or positional scheme.
Implement skip sets as validated zero-based transformer block indices; conditional execution never inherits negative-branch skipping.
Compare intermediate tensors at first, middle and final blocks, text refinement and final velocity; include non-square images and unequal prompt lengths.
Serves: native MOSS denoising.
Disappears: model-specific Python serving and duplicate matrix/attention machinery through tensor/graphruntime/CUDA reuse.
Evidence: block and complete-forward numerical comparisons consumed by sampling and performance work.
Batch: graph/kernel/media lanes; refresh kernel identities where changed, expire inference guards and reconcile model recipe dependencies.
TestMOSSExistingGraphSITUReference composes existing Scale, Tanh, Sigmoid and Multiply operations.
The reference executor matches all seven upstream FP32 SITU values exactly and rejects ordinary SwiGLU substitution.
This probe does not establish BF16, device or complete-transformer parity.

items.title: Preserve custom schedule, seeded noise and guidance

budget.reason: The shared CPU RNG draft adds 483 production syntax nodes after deleting the RAE-owned implementation and migrating its serving consumer. The original 600-node allowance remains for schedule and trajectory integration.

steps.title: Match every denoising step and its actual schedule
steps.rationale:
Implement nearest-training-grid sigma snapping, tie direction, unique-consecutive removal and terminal handling from MOSSImageScheduler.
Do not substitute an ordinary FlowMatchEuler scheduler or apply shift twice.
Preserve fp32 Gaussian generation, separate prediction casts before CFG, Euler accumulation and negative-branch skip 22 over the configured interval.
Prove default two-forward behavior, guidance 1, skipping disabled, custom negative text and short schedules whose snapped count differs from the requested count.
Bind exact CPU-generator noise through existing torchrng or accept externally supplied golden latents; any alternate RNG is a separately declared mode.
Reject nonfinite settings, invalid skip indices, empty prompt masks and invalid dimensions.
Serves: deterministic request semantics and faithful generation.
Disappears: handwritten model-specific timestep and guidance paths through existing sampler ownership.
Evidence: schedule/noise/CFG and per-step latent records read by decoder and final parity.
Batch: sampling/media lanes; expire inference guards and reconcile generation policy identity.
Reuse assessment finds an existing CPU MT19937 normal generator in rae and a CUDA Philox generator in torchrng.
The unchanged CPU implementation is numerically close but not bit-identical to the frozen MOSS CPU-noise fixtures.
Do not substitute CUDA Philox or claim bitwise CPU-seed agreement from approximate RAE noise tests.
Consolidate a corrected CPU generator under torchrng with both RAE and MOSS consumers when its numerical contract is proven.
The retained reuse evidence corpus is dataset:sha256:061bdd6fe0f4be62f84a2dab832b027bad6d7f2ab90950a8a23905c57a5c98f1 with 53 members.
The nearest-grid draft matches all 1342 captured sigma and timestep values for requests of 1, 2, 50 and 1001 steps exactly.
The 1001-step request deduplicates to 616 actual steps.
TestMOSSNearestGridScheduleReference also checks first and final primitive Euler states against the frozen dtype policy.
The pinned PyTorch linspace source uses two-ended float32 arithmetic.

items.title: Decode packed MOSS latents through the FLUX.2 VAE

budget.reason: Support the small decoder and batch-normalized packed latents in existing image/graph owners; reuse convolution, normalization and attention primitives.

steps.title: Match latent unpacking, decoder output and pixels
steps.rationale:
Apply stored batch-normalization mean and variance with the pinned epsilon to the 128-channel latents before the exact 2-by-2 unpack into 32 channels.
Load the bundled AutoencoderKLFlux2 small decoder, including post-quant convolution, decoder blocks, normalization and mid-block attention in fp32.
Match clamping, range conversion, tensor layout, rounding and encoded image behavior to the chosen oracle output contract.
Do not reuse QwenImage VAE normalization or assume identical FLUX decoder channel widths.
Compare unpacked tensors, decoder boundaries, floating RGB and final pixel output on square and rectangular inputs.
Serves: usable generated images.
Disappears: a separate VAE process; reuse latentimage/diffusionimage primitives where numerical contracts match.
Evidence: VAE and pixel goldens consumed by native end-to-end parity and UI rendering.
Batch: convolution/graph/media lanes; expire inference guards and reconcile decoder artifact dependencies.

items.title: Connect components into a cancellable resident inference session

budget.reason: Compose existing graph, residency and media session owners; no parallel executor or resource manager.

steps.title: Execute complete image requests through native recipes
steps.rationale:
Compose conditioning, denoising and decoding using resident graph bindings and existing admission accounting.
Keep latent, prediction, guidance and Euler buffers on the device across steps; transfer output only for declared observation or final publication.
Separate model loading, prompt encoding, denoising, decoding and publication measurements using existing run records.
Release temporary allocations and leases on success, failure and cancellation, and prevent cancelled work from publishing a completed image.
Cover concurrent requests, cold/warm reuse, SFT selection and reload, resource refusal and cancellation at each stage with small device fixtures.
Serves: complete native inference and responsive cancellation.
Disappears: per-step host transfers and duplicated session orchestration through graphruntime and mediacapability.
Evidence: lifecycle, transfer and stage records consumed by UI and full-model evaluation.
Batch: graph/runtime/media lanes; expire inference guards, update recipe and media bindings together.

items.title: Expose model import and image generation through existing UI/API

budget.reason: Extend library and generation schemas and views with capability-derived controls; no new application or MOSS-specific route family.

steps.title: Publish image capabilities and request provenance
steps.rationale:
Register the pinned MOSS-Image-SFT checkpoint as the image-generation target with verified component identities and ModelScope provenance.
Extend existing generation operations with prompt, dimensions, seed, steps, guidance and negative prompt; encode policy defaults in the selected recipe.
Accept serialized layout prompts without changing whitespace or Unicode after the request is committed; structured input, if offered, uses one defined serialization and validates centered yxyx coordinates against the canvas.
Reject unsupported training, editing and SLG requests explicitly.
Bind output to checkpoint, tokenizer/template, import description, recipe, sampling settings and input identity; report pending, failed and cancelled states accurately.
Serves: discoverable, reproducible image generation.
Disappears: model-name dispatch and duplicated API defaults through existing capability and generation ownership.
Evidence: request/response and artifact tests feed API manifest and compatibility publication.
Batch: server/media/schema lanes; expire guards as required and regenerate public/media contracts through their owners.

steps.title: Finish the library-to-image user journey
steps.rationale:
Reuse Library import and the Generation view for acquisition progress, component reuse, readiness, model choice, prompt input, image size, generate, cancel, preview and download.
Show clear progress through model loading, prompt processing, image generation and decoding; advanced sampling options stay secondary.
Expose layout input as an optional prompt mode with a simple example and clear coordinate errors, not a new canvas editor.
Show resource refusal and recovery without leaving controls stuck or claiming success for incomplete work.
Browser acceptance covers import readiness, SFT selection, normal and layout generation, preview/download, invalid inputs, cancellation and retry using hermetic operations; real model evidence remains in the cycle.
Serves: an understandable image-generation workflow.
Disappears: bespoke Gradio/ComfyUI dependency and duplicate UI orchestration through current library/generation views.
Evidence: browser-lane journey record and operation provenance reused by closeout.
Batch: web UI and server lanes; media/API reconciliation follows schema changes, and browser checks run only in the required lane.

items.title: Reduce repeated work and peak memory without changing the default model

budget.reason: Use existing cache, graph and resource owners; add only identity and residency support demonstrated by measured repeated work.

steps.title: Measure and improve whole-request resource use
steps.rationale:
Establish cold/warm time and peak host/device memory before optimization with matching inputs and output contracts.
Prefer stage residency: encode once, release the conditioner, retain transformer weights through denoising, then decode; use bounded block streaming only where admission requires it.
Cache prompt conditioning and deterministic text refinement only with complete model/tokenizer/template/input/dtype/policy identities and bounded eviction; reuse across models or revisions requires identical component identities.
Reuse scratch buffers and graph programs, avoid materializing dense attention matrices, and key graph reuse by shape, prompt length, branch policy and resource lifetime.
VAE tiling must prove correct boundary behavior and no seams; quantization, reduced steps or resolution are explicit quality-changing modes, not an invisible way to claim parity or speed.
Measure actual GPU allocation lifetimes, transfer bytes, host RSS and time per stage; admission includes workspace and graph allocations.
Verify cache invalidation, budget adherence and cancellation with small fixtures; the model cycle measures performance and quality against the frozen baseline.
Serves: lower latency and memory under the same default generation contract.
Disappears: repeated component loading, recomputation and allocation through existing graph/residency/cache owners.
Evidence: comparable baseline/candidate records with required quality cells, consumed by final evaluation and resource guidance.
Batch: runtime/media/kernel lanes; batch execution-surface changes before refreshing guards and reusing model evidence.

items.title: Demonstrate model import reuse beyond MOSS

budget.reason: The second real consumer justifies only the shared intake mechanics it exercises; remove its replaced manual path in the same change.

steps.title: Run the deterministic importer on an existing supported family
steps.rationale:
Use the existing Krea2 multi-component image profile as the second consumer and an existing single-file GGUF intake as a regression control.
Keep Krea's Qwen3-VL conditioner, selected-layer fusion, QwenImage VAE and scheduler facts distinct from MOSS; share acquisition, inventory, validation, recipe materialization and lifecycle only where the contracts match.
Use small representative checkpoint fixtures to prove reproducible canonical identities, explicit unsupported-operator reports and idempotent restart across both image families.
Remove the displaced manual importer glue and duplicated fixture scaffolding in the same landing.
The importer supports declared profiles; adding a wholly new architecture still requires an audited numerical implementation and independent evidence.
Serves: mechanized model onboarding across Overgo.
Disappears: repeated family-specific intake code through existing shared owners, with concrete deleted paths recorded in the landing.
Evidence: cross-family import and legacy compatibility records used by the final campaign assessment.
Batch: intake/profile lanes; inference guards move only if recipe execution changes; reconcile media mappings if affected.
Component-local identities must exclude sibling component numbering.
TestImageComponentIdentityExcludesSiblingLayout reproduces a changed decoder identity when only a transformer policy is added to the parent model.

The regression check passes with the correction and retains identity across reversed enumeration.

Apply this correction with the Krea inventory migration and retain predecessor manifests and activations for rollback.
The controlled test proves component identity behavior and does not establish full-model execution or shared device residency.

items.title: Validate the SFT model and publish honest capability evidence

budget.reason: Extend current evaluation protocols and compatibility records; no standalone benchmark service or scorecard.

steps.title: Compare native SFT inference with the pinned SFT oracle
steps.rationale:
Add full-model cycle coverage for the ModelScope SFT checkpoint over the frozen prompt, layout, language, size, negative-prompt and seed matrix.
Require stage tolerances and end-to-end output acceptance independently; pleasing pictures or finite tensors alone are insufficient.
Evaluate rendered text and layout adherence on a frozen held-out set, preserving independent human or established metric judgments where needed.
Bind every result to exact implementation, source, checkpoint, recipe, suite and environment identities; unavailable devices or missing artifacts remain missing evidence.
Publish image-generation capability verification only after required cells complete; do not advertise training capability.
Serves: trustworthy native model support.
Disappears: unverified support labels through existing evaluation and activation evidence.
Evidence: retained native-versus-upstream stage and quality records read by activation, compatibility and closeout.
Batch: evaluation/claim lanes; full-model work runs in the cycle, after all execution-surface changes and guard renewal.

steps.title: Measure latency and memory on supported hardware
steps.rationale:
Compare native and pinned upstream runs with equal checkpoint, prompt, image size, guidance, actual step schedule, precision and quality requirements.
Report cold acquisition/load separately from warm generation; include prompt encoding, transformer time, decoder time, wall-clock latency, peak host/GPU memory and transfer volume.
Measure resident and bounded-memory modes at 1024 square and a rectangular case, plus the largest admitted case established by evidence.
Record hardware and warmup/repeat protocol before comparing results; do not invent a consumer-GPU fit claim from weight size alone.
A faster setting that changes precision, step count or image size gets its own quality/performance record.
Serves: measurable capability under realistic memory constraints.
Disappears: unsupported speed or memory claims through existing benchmark/evaluation records.
Evidence: one resource comparison record reused by UI guidance, documentation and closeout.
Batch: cycle-only model evaluation; unchanged execution identities permit evidence reuse without rerunning the landing gate.
